title: Orsen and the House
premise: Odile Thornbury, a hospice nurse who has spent his life refusing to believe in anything he cannot chart, takes a night shift at Verrin House, a private estate where the dying patients count backwards in unison. As the house's mirrors begin lagging behind reality by one second, Odile learns the family invited something in decades ago to cheat death, and it has been collecting ever since. To survive until sunrise, he must uncover which member of the household made the bargain and decide whether justice means exposing them or finishing what they started. In the end, Odile breaks his own rule and believes, paying for his survival by taking the debt onto himself as dawn arrives.
about_author: Oscar Nakamura is a former night-shift caregiver who turned to horror after years of listening to what patients say at 3 a.m. He writes from a farmhouse with no mirrors in the bedrooms.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He arrives at Verrin House for a temporary hospice contract, professionally skeptical of the staff's whispers about the east wing. He hears three dying patients counting backwards in perfect unison and files it under shared delirium. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a night round, he notices his reflection in a hallway mirror raises its hand after he does. He tests every mirror in the house; all of them lag exactly one second. Emotional beat: rational explanations stacking up and failing.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The housekeeper, Mrs. Aldous, gives him a laminated list of rules: cover the mirrors after midnight, never answer the intercom, don't enter the east wing. She refuses to say who wrote them. Emotional beat: dread disguised as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: The Family Album
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Searching for patient records, he finds photographs of the Verrin family spanning a century, each generation posing identically before the same mirror, each with one face scratched out. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: What the Dying Know
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Odile and patient Eleanor Verrin, 94. Eleanor stops counting long enough to tell him the house was 'paid in advance' and that she intends to die owing nothing. Emotional beat: first genuine human connection.

chapters.title: Intercom
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At 3:07 a.m. the dead intercom crackles with his own voice asking to be let in. He doesn't answer. The doorknob turns anyway. Emotional beat: terror without evidence he can report.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Eleanor's POV. A flashback chapter: in 1968, her father bargained with something in the cellar to save her mother, trading 'a life per generation.' Eleanor has spent her life preparing to default on the loan. Emotional beat: guilt inherited like furniture.

chapters.title: The East Wing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Breaking the last rule, he enters the sealed wing and finds a room of covered mirrors, all uncovered, all reflecting him a full second early now. Something is arriving before he does. Emotional beat: inversion; the house is ahead of him.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldous Confesses
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The housekeeper admits she isn't staff; she's the granddaughter of the man who brokered the original bargain, kept alive past her time as collateral. She begs Odile to leave before sunrise. Emotional beat: pity entangled with self-preservation.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. All the patients count backwards together through the walls, synchronized, descending toward zero. Staff flee; Odile stays because Eleanor grips his wrist and won't let go. Emotional beat: loyalty against instinct.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The count reaches zero. Every mirror in the house shows rooms that aren't there, filled with people wearing the faces of the scratched-out photographs. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into fear.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A figure made of lagging reflections appears in the east wing, courteous and patient, presenting an itemized account of lives owed. It offers Odile the same deal the family got: name a substitute. Emotional beat: temptation framed as kindness.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He researches the family's history and discovers the original bargain was made to escape prosecution for a death they caused. The entity wasn't invited to cheat mortality but to dodge justice, and it has been collecting interest ever since. Emotional beat: moral clarity hardening.

chapters.title: Eleanor Refuses
chapters.summary: Eleanor's POV. Offered one more extension if she names Odile as payment, Eleanor declines, choosing to die owing nothing. Her countdown resumes, faster now. Emotional beat: dignity as defiance.

chapters.title: The Cellar Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the ledger's clues, he descends to the cellar where the bargain was struck and finds the original contract written in a family Bible, with a clause no one ever read aloud: the debt can be transferred only by consent. Emotional beat: hope with a knife hidden in it.

chapters.title: Aldous's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldous's POV. Desperate to be released from her century of borrowed time, she attempts to sign the transfer herself without consent from the other party. The mirrors reject her; she begins aging rapidly, seconds at a time. Emotional beat: tragedy of shortcuts.

chapters.title: Sunrise Negotiation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With dawn forty minutes away, Odile confronts the Collector with the contract clause and demands terms: the family's debt audited honestly, not collected by fear. The Collector agrees to hear one counteroffer. Emotional beat: nerve stretched to snapping.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The truth surfaces fully: the thing in the house is the accumulated guilt of everyone who let it stay, given shape by invitation after invitation. It is powerful only because generations kept feeding it silence. Emotional beat: revelation as accusation.

chapters.title: The Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile offers himself, not as prey but as witness: someone who will remember, record, and testify to every life the house took, ending the silence that sustains it. The Collector hesitates, because being seen is the one price it cannot pay. Emotional beat: courage as refusal to look away.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Sunrise floods the mirrors; the lag collapses to zero. Eleanor dies peacefully owing nothing. The Collector withdraws into the east wing, diminished, waiting for the next invitation. Odile survives, changed. Emotional beat: exhausted relief shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Weeks later, Odile publishes an anonymous account of Verrin House. He finds his own reflection now lags everywhere, everywhere, one second late, the mark of a man who saw and stayed. He accepts it as his fee. Emotional beat: bittersweet reckoning.

chapters.title: Invitation Open
chapters.summary: Final chapter, omniscient POV. A new hospice nurse receives a lucrative contract at another old estate, rules laminated and waiting. Somewhere, a mirror runs one second slow. The cycle asks again. Emotional beat: quiet, unresolved dread.
